title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 100: Calling of extraordinary general meeting

content.overview: Section 100 permits the Board to call an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) and gives members meeting the statutory voting threshold a requisition route. If the Board fails to act within the statutory timetable, requisitionists may call and hold the meeting subject to the section’s conditions.
content.glance: The Board may call an EGM. Members meeting the one-tenth statutory voting threshold may requisition one; after Board default, they may call it themselves within the section’s timetable. This section does not apply to an OPC: see section 122(1) and its separate procedure.
content.study:
## Operative rule
The Board may call an EGM whenever it considers fit. Subject to the statutory exception for a wholly owned subsidiary of a company incorporated outside India, an EGM must be held at a place within India.

Members may requisition an EGM if they meet the threshold in section 100(2): for a company with share capital, not less than one-tenth of the paid-up share capital carrying voting rights; for a company without share capital, not less than one-tenth of the total voting power of members entitled to vote. The requisition must identify the matters for consideration, be signed by the requisitionists, and be sent to the registered office.

If the Board does not, within 21 days after receiving a valid requisition, proceed to call the meeting for the stated matter on a day no later than 45 days after receipt, the requisitionists may call and hold it themselves within three months of the requisition. They must follow the same manner in which the Board calls and holds a meeting. Reasonable expenses may be reimbursed by the company and dealt with as section 100(6) provides.

## Application checklist
Verify the company’s capital structure and voting rights on the date the requisition is received; calculate the threshold; ensure the requisition states the business, is signed, and reaches the registered office; then calculate the 21-day, 45-day and three-month periods separately. Check applicable rules and company-specific exemptions before advising.

## One Person Company limitation
Section 122(1) expressly provides that sections 98 and 100–111 do not apply to a One Person Company (OPC). Do not apply this section’s ordinary meeting mechanics to an OPC as if it were an ordinary company. Section 122(2)–(3) separately governs how ordinary business that would otherwise be transacted at an AGM is handled for an OPC. Confirm OPC status and apply the current section 122 procedure before advising.

sections.heading: Board’s power and place of meeting
sections.body: The Board may call an EGM whenever it considers fit. The section’s place-of-meeting proviso generally requires an EGM to be held in India, subject to its stated wholly-owned-subsidiary exception.

sections.heading: Member threshold and valid requisition
sections.body: The threshold is at least one-tenth of the paid-up share capital carrying voting rights for a company with share capital, or at least one-tenth of total voting power for a company without share capital. The requisition must state the matters, be signed, and be sent to the registered office.

sections.heading: Board default and requisitionists’ meeting
sections.body: The Board has 21 days to proceed to call the meeting for a date no later than 45 days after receipt of the valid requisition. On default, requisitionists may call and hold it within three months of the requisition, following the statutory manner.

sections.heading: Expenses and verification limits
sections.body: Reasonable expenses of the requisitionists’ meeting may be reimbursed by the company and dealt with as section 100(6) provides. Verify the applicable rules, current amendments, articles and company-specific exemptions.

sections.heading: One Person Company limitation
sections.body: Section 122(1) disapplies sections 98 and 100–111 to an OPC. Section 122(2)–(3) supplies a separate procedure for ordinary business otherwise transacted at an AGM. Confirm whether the company is an OPC before applying this section.

provisions.title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 100: Calling of extraordinary general meeting

examples.title: Threshold met
examples.body: Members holding at least the section 100(2) threshold send a signed requisition identifying the business to the registered office. The company must assess it under the statutory process and timetable.

examples.title: Threshold or form defective
examples.body: A group counts shares that do not carry voting rights or sends a request that does not identify the matters for consideration. The statutory threshold or requisition requirements may not be met; do not assume the special self-help route has arisen.

hypotheticals.question: Members satisfying the one-tenth threshold deliver a signed requisition to the registered office. The Board takes no step within 21 days and no meeting is scheduled within the statutory 45-day period. May the members call the EGM themselves?
hypotheticals.analysis: Apply section 100(2)–(5): first verify threshold, date and validity of the requisition, then the Board’s failure to proceed within 21 days to a meeting date no later than 45 days, and whether the requisitionists call and hold the meeting within three months and follow the required manner. The conclusion depends on the proved dates and compliance.

distinctions.title: Section 100 and connected meeting-compliance requirements
distinctions.right: Section 100 concerns the authority and procedure for calling an EGM. Section 101 separately governs notice; section 102 concerns the explanatory statement for special business; section 103 governs quorum.
